raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, an unfinished DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill chunk keeps one decoder-replay row instead of `min(query_len, 128)`. The finishing chunk, decode, and prompt-logprobs stay on the window. CUDA is unchanged. #59039 is the 128-row path this trims.

## Claims

- An unfinished chunk is `num_computed_prefill_tokens + query_len < prefill_len`. On ROCm its kept length is 1. Prompt-logprobs still keep every row.
- An empty `decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes` on ROCm also captures `[1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96]` below the window. An explicit list that omits 1 is rejected. CUDA still starts at the window.
- 8k prompts are one chunk, so both arms replay 128 rows. At 256k the unfinished chunks are shorter.

## Validation

4× MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, ROCm 7.2.3, nightly. `vllm bench serve`, random data, 20 prompts, one warmup, output length 1024. The one-row arm passed the capture list explicitly because the empty list started at 128.

| Shape | Metric | Baseline | One-row | Δ |
|----|----|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 8k→1k MC2, DSpark, seed 7 | TTFT (ms) | 336.2 | 337.1 | +0.3% |
| | TPOT (ms) | 3.96 | 4.03 | +1.8% |
| | E2E (ms) | 4466.9 | 4493.2 | +0.6% |
| | Output (tok/s) | 431.1 | 430.2 | −0.2% |
| 8k→1k MC2, no DSpark, seed 7 | TTFT (ms) | 463.2 | 463.7 | +0.1% |
| | TPOT (ms) | 11.67 | 11.63 | −0.3% |
| | E2E (ms) | 12339.3 | 12353.3 | +0.1% |
| | Output (tok/s) | 165.8 | 165.7 | −0.0% |
| 8k→1k MC6, DSpark, seed 9 | TTFT (ms) | 1075.7 | 1068.3 | −0.7% |
| | TPOT (ms) | 6.22 | 6.29 | +1.1% |
| | E2E (ms) | 7651.2 | 7435.6 | −2.8% |
| | Output (tok/s) | 699.8 | 714.8 | +2.1% |
| 256k→1k MC2, DSpark, seed 7 | TTFT (ms) | 13109.6 | 12181.2 | −7.1% |
| | TPOT (ms) | 7.94 | 8.27 | +4.2% |
| | E2E (ms) | 21452.2 | 20810.7 | −3.0% |
| | Output (tok/s) | 95.5 | 98.2 | +2.9% |
| 256k→1k MC8, DSpark, seed 10 | TTFT (ms) | 23984.5 | 22806.5 | −4.9% |
| | TPOT (ms) | 47.31 | 45.71 | −3.4% |
| | E2E (ms) | 73091.2 | 70222.7 | −3.9% |
| | Output (tok/s) | 109.3 | 113.5 | +3.9% |

TPOT excludes the first token, so it measures decode, which still keeps `min(query_len, window)`. On 256k MC2 the median rises 0.33 ms (mean 7.81 → 7.71 ms, P99 11.88 → 11.47 ms). End-to-end latency falls because the unfinished prefill chunks are shorter.

One incomplete 16k chunk, median replay launch: 9.45 ms with 128 rows, 1.80 ms with 1 row (`0.31.1rc1.dev23+g43b4aaea3`).

GSM8K 5-shot, n=1319, probabilistic DSpark, one-row arm only: 0.9196, against published off scores 0.9272 / 0.9265. RULER `niah_single_2` at 16384 is 1.0 and finishes in one chunk. The same task at 131072, n=500, TP4, synthetic DSpark, on the nightly with the one-row changes applied, shows no regression against the 128-row path.

pytest covers the ROCm row rule and the capture sizes below the window. gfx942 only. CUDA was not measured.

<details>
<summary>Serve and bench</summary>

```bash
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4

vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8014 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 266240 \
  --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-log-requests \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"greedy","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.9,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5],"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

</details>

## Details

`model_state.py` applies the one-row limit only on ROCm. `decoder_replay_cudagraph.py` adds the sizes below the window. Kept lengths stay on the host, so this adds no device sync.

Depends on #59039 (already merged).

nodes.body: Thanks for catching this @ischencheng. I see #62817 now implements the far-from-end gate plus handling for the following chunk. Do you intend that PR to supersede this one, or would you prefer me to adapt the same fix here for ROCm? I can also validate #62817 on gfx942 against current main

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @frida-andersson.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork
Superseded by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62817. I will close this PR once that gets merged

This drops rows that a later step still reads.

```python
# L133, _gather_replay_batch_kernel
if kept_end - kept_begin < end - begin:
    kv_start = tl.maximum(kv_start, tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + req) - window)
```

The finishing chunk only gets this floor when it is trimmed. Otherwise its first row attends 127 rows back into the previous chunk, and with one row kept those replay-layer KV slots were never written. Two ways to hit it:

- The finish is <= 128 rows. Your new test is one: 250 = 200 + 50, row 200 reads 73-198 after chunk 1 kept only row 199.
- The finish runs in a FULL graph, or a PIECEWISE graph below `decoder_replay_trim_threshold`. `_prepare_replay_batch` returns at L462 there, and the replay layers run on every row with the batch's SWA metadata. E.g. 8192 + 300: the 300-token finish plus a few decodes takes a small PIECEWISE graph and reads rows 8065-8191.

Could we keep one row only when the rest of the prompt is out of the finish's reach? Something like:

```python
remaining = prefill_len - computed - query_lens
# The finish may run untrimmed up to the trim threshold and reads window - 1 rows back.
reach = (layers.trim_threshold or self.max_num_tokens) + int(layers.window)
row_limit = np.where(unfinished & (remaining >= reach), 1, int(layers.window))
```

That keeps the 128-row tail on the last chunk or two, so a 256K prompt still skips almost all of them.

Checked on an L4 with this PR's own fixtures (`_input_batch` / `_prepare`): for 250 = 200 + 50 and for 1024 + 300 (finish padded to 320 in PIECEWISE), chunk 1 writes only its last row and the finish needs 126 rows nobody wrote. With the snippet above chunk 1 writes 128 rows, nothing is missing, and a 1024-token chunk of a 100K prompt still keeps one row.
nodes.diffHunk:
@@ -462,10 +464,19 @@ def _prepare_replay_batch(
 
         num_reqs = input_batch.num_reqs
         query_lens = np.diff(input_batch.query_start_loc_np[: num_reqs + 1])
+        # is_prefilling stays true on the finishing chunk.
+        row_limit: int | np.ndarray = layers.window
+        if current_platform.is_rocm():
+            computed = input_batch.num_computed_prefill_tokens_np[:num_reqs]
+            prefill_len = input_batch.prefill_len_np[:num_reqs]
+            unfinished = input_batch.is_prefilling_np[:num_reqs] & (
+                computed + query_lens < prefill_len
+            )
+            row_limit = np.where(unfinished, 1, int(layers.window))

inline_comments.body:
This drops rows that a later step still reads.

```python
# L133, _gather_replay_batch_kernel
if kept_end - kept_begin < end - begin:
    kv_start = tl.maximum(kv_start, tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + req) - window)
```

The finishing chunk only gets this floor when it is trimmed. Otherwise its first row attends 127 rows back into the previous chunk, and with one row kept those replay-layer KV slots were never written. Two ways to hit it:

- The finish is <= 128 rows. Your new test is one: 250 = 200 + 50, row 200 reads 73-198 after chunk 1 kept only row 199.
- The finish runs in a FULL graph, or a PIECEWISE graph below `decoder_replay_trim_threshold`. `_prepare_replay_batch` returns at L462 there, and the replay layers run on every row with the batch's SWA metadata. E.g. 8192 + 300: the 300-token finish plus a few decodes takes a small PIECEWISE graph and reads rows 8065-8191.

Could we keep one row only when the rest of the prompt is out of the finish's reach? Something like:

```python
remaining = prefill_len - computed - query_lens
# The finish may run untrimmed up to the trim threshold and reads window - 1 rows back.
reach = (layers.trim_threshold or self.max_num_tokens) + int(layers.window)
row_limit = np.where(unfinished & (remaining >= reach), 1, int(layers.window))
```

That keeps the 128-row tail on the last chunk or two, so a 256K prompt still skips almost all of them.

Checked on an L4 with this PR's own fixtures (`_input_batch` / `_prepare`): for 250 = 200 + 50 and for 1024 + 300 (finish padded to 320 in PIECEWISE), chunk 1 writes only its last row and the finish needs 126 rows nobody wrote. With the snippet above chunk 1 writes 128 rows, nothing is missing, and a 1024-token chunk of a 100K prompt still keeps one row.
